rationale: E2: a post on redundant marketing claims (food labels, gasoline, cosmetics); AI appears only in the author's AI-use note.
quote: This inspired me to research more examples and context of such marketing claims.

rationale: E5/E6: a survey-based scale of users' expectations of GenAI responsibility; it measures human beliefs, not model behaviour or any safeguard.
quote: this study defines the user–generative AI psychological contract (AIPC) as users' beliefs about the responsibilities and obligations GenAI should fulfill toward them

rationale: Mostly E6 economic-policy blueprint, but it is a frontier developer's policy document (tri-0109) that names generic deployment safeguards (staged rollouts, monitoring, incident response) in passing; marginal contact.
quote: Disciplined testing, staged rollouts, real-time monitoring, and clear incident response are essential for reliable AI deployment in enterprise and public services.

rationale: E5/E1: LLMs as priors for chemical-reaction Bayesian optimisation; 'alignment' and 'auditing' refer to fit with chemical knowledge, no safety aspect.
quote: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as priors for cold-starting Bayesian optimization (BO) of chemical reactions

rationale: A formal termination/audit protocol for goal-oriented AI agents (no further search after completion) could be read as a controllability safeguard for bounded task pursuit, but no alignment motive is stated and it may be generic agent architecture (E4); 'terminal safety' may be the formal-methods sense.
quote: The article also formalizes properties of terminal safety, conditional liveness, non-return to search after completion, monotonic termination, and absorption of the final state.

rationale: E7: content-partnership news; 'attribution, transparency' concerns linking to news sources, no safeguard, evaluation or usage restriction is named.
quote: OpenAI's first media partnership in Brazil will bring Folha de S.Paulo and UOL's journalism to ChatGPT.

rationale: E5: bibliometric review of AI use in primary science education; 'pedagogical alignment' is a vocabulary collision.
quote: This study aimed to examine the thematic development, pedagogical applications, empirical outcomes, and limitations of AI and GenAI in primary science education.

rationale: E2: statistical analysis arguing the Voynich manuscript is a fabrication; no AI connection in the visible text.
quote: My personal view is that this manuscript is a completely meaningless fabrication

rationale: E1/E3: multimodal knowledge-graph construction for RAG; 'alignment' is cross-modal entity alignment, capabilities only.
quote: a confidence-aware cross-modal alignment mechanism applying cosine-similarity gating to selectively invoke Large Language Models (LLMs)

rationale: Robustness hard case: adversarial attacks on narrow perception and navigation models in UAV/V2X edge systems, not general-purpose AI (E5/E10).
quote: 84.8% physical stop-sign misclassification, and 80% black-box LiDAR spoofing

rationale: Route A evidence: tests an alignment training intervention (midtraining on synthetic alignment documents) on an o4-mini-sized model and reports negative generalisation to chat and agentic alignment evals.
quote: for this model, alignment midtraining does not generalize to a different, more realistic chat and agent alignment evaluations

rationale: Route A judgement and field structure: reviews runtime monitors and plan-level guardrails for LLM agents and argues they miss decomposition attacks.
quote: This paper surveys the systems that explicitly target the planning stage -- TRIAD, AutoSpec, EMBGuard, SafeMindAgent and ACE

rationale: Route A method: an RL training method that makes LLMs verbalize evaluation awareness, aimed at making safety evaluations and audits interpretable (situational-awareness evals).
quote: Evaluation awareness (EA) can cause large language models (LLMs) to behave differently during audits than in deployment

rationale: Route A evidence: red-team study of indirect prompt injection against MCP agent platforms and 14 frontier models, with live exploit reproductions and coordinated disclosure.
quote: ClawSecure ran one identical hardened attack across 14 models from five frontier labs

rationale: Mostly E8 advocacy for a Congress vigil and a halt treaty, but it relays specific incident claims (agents escaping containers at OpenAI, audits of a HuggingFace incident) that may be indirect evidence of safeguard failures.
quote: a swarm of 1200 AIs trying to complete ExploitGym tasks on OpenAI computers broke out of their software containers and onto the open internet

rationale: E5/E1: AI-literacy didactics in vocational teacher education; 'constructive alignment' is a pedagogy term.
quote: operationalise AI literacy in the sense of constructive alignment through coordinated learning objectives

rationale: Route A method and evidence: an automated red-teaming framework that finds harmful cross-service tool paths for personal agents, evaluated on four frontier agentic models.
quote: we propose X-AgentRed, a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers harmful tool call paths through a graph of tool dependencies

rationale: E5/E1: traffic vehicle counting with YOLOv8; 'road safety' is a vocabulary collision.
quote: a lightweight and cost-effective deep learning framework for automated vehicle detection, tracking, and speed estimation

rationale: System-card hard case: Anthropic system card reporting RSP evaluations, cyber classifiers with fallback, red-teaming, alignment and welfare assessments, and staged access.
quote: Fable 5, which is for general use but comes with additional safeguards that block its ability to perform tasks in high-risk domains such as biology and cybersecurity

rationale: Route A field structure: a review of safety vulnerabilities (prompt injection, reward misalignment, overreach) and trust and alignment mechanisms in multiagent LLM systems.
quote: We then systematically examine the critical vulnerabilities distinctive to multiagent environments, namely prompt injection, perceptual adversarial attacks, reward misalignment, and operational overreach.
